# Lessons

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-lesson-index.sh — do not edit by hand.
     The source of truth is the `# lesson:` and `# summary:` header
     lines in each example/learn/*.tesl file. Change those, then run the
     script. `--check` runs in the gate, so drift fails CI. -->

Every lesson is a small runnable `.tesl` file with its explanation inline,
and every one is also a regression test — each has a committed byte-exact
`.rkt` snapshot and test blocks in the gate. Read one with:

```bash
tesl help manual <lesson-name>      # e.g. tesl help manual lesson05-intro-to-proofs
```

There are **81** lessons. That number is generated; it cannot drift.

## In a hurry? Start with these

A why-Tesl showcase rather than a build-your-first-API path — read them cold,
in any order. Each one shows a thing no other language in this space does.
For building something end to end, follow the full sequence below instead, or
start from [Getting Started](GETTING-STARTED.md) and [Your first change](first-change.md).

| Lesson | Shows |
|---|---|
| [`lesson00-hello-world`](../example/learn/lesson00-hello-world.tesl) | Write, compile and run your first Tesl module — module, exposing, import, fn and interpolated strings |
| [`lesson05-intro-to-proofs`](../example/learn/lesson05-intro-to-proofs.tesl) | A check function stamps a value as validated, and the stamp travels with it through the type system |
| [`lesson12-records-with-proofs`](../example/learn/lesson12-records-with-proofs.tesl) | Put a proof on a record field, so the data shape itself guarantees its contents were validated |
| [`lesson14-test-blocks`](../example/learn/lesson14-test-blocks.tesl) | Write tests inside the language with test blocks, including randomized property runs |
| [`lesson18-database-sql-and-proofs`](../example/learn/lesson18-database-sql-and-proofs.tesl) | Declare a table with entity and query it in typed SQL whose results carry a proof that they came from the database |
| [`lesson64-password-storage`](../example/learn/lesson64-password-storage.tesl) | Store and verify a password safely in two calls, with no cryptographic choices left to get wrong |
| [`lesson68-server-endpoints-as-tools`](../example/learn/lesson68-server-endpoints-as-tools.tesl) | Hand an agent every endpoint the caller's own proof already covers, as preauthenticated tools |
| [`lesson72-units`](../example/learn/lesson72-units.tesl) | Give physical quantities compile-time dimensions, checked when you multiply and erased at runtime |

## The full sequence

**Reading order is value order**: if you get through *N* lessons in an hour,
the first *N* are the *N* that matter most. Where a lesson builds on an earlier
one it says so, with the one-line reason — so you can jump in anywhere and know
exactly what you are missing.
